name: ht
why: A terminal hex editor and disassembler for executables that lets you walk through binary structure, a classic door into reverse engineering.

brief.what_it_is: HT (HT Editor, ht) is a terminal-based viewer, editor and analyzer for text, binary and especially executable files. You point it at a file and it shows the raw bytes in a hex view, or parses the file's structure (headers, sections, symbols, imports, relocations) and disassembles its code. It can also run a code and data analyser over the image, add labels and comments, search with regex or expressions, and run block operations that rewrite bytes. It reads many executable formats (ELF, PE32/PE64, Mach-O, MZ, NE, LE, COFF, XBE, PEF, Java class) and writes changes back to the file.
brief.why_it_exists: HT is a free-software tool for inspecting and modifying executables, which the README calls 'a file viewer, editor and analyzer for text, binary, and (especially) executable files'. The homepage frames it as a classic reverse-engineering tool, and the scout note calls it a door into reverse engineering.
brief.how_it_works: The loader parses the file's format, then the code and data analyser follows branch sources and destinations recursively, finds procedure entries, and creates labels and xrefs. You can extend the analysis by hand: press 'c' to continue code analysis at the cursor, 'n' to name an address, and '#' to add comments. Search and block operations use a built-in expression evaluator with functions such as readbyte(ofs) and readstring(ofs, size), and analysis state is saved in a FILENAME.htcfg file beside the target.

commands_seen.context: Short form of --version: shows version and copyright on the console.
Long form of -v: shows version and copyright on the console.
Short form of --text: loads the file(s) in text editor mode.
Long form of -t: loads the file(s) in text editor mode.
Short form of --bin: loads the file(s) in hex editor mode.
Long form of -b: loads the file(s) in hex editor mode.
Short form of --auto: tries to guess the file type.
Long form of -a: tries to guess the file type.

brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was shown in the brew data or the README. Config is created automatically on first run: ~/.htcfg2 on Unix and ht.cfg2 next to ht.exe on Windows. Per-file analyser state goes in FILENAME.htcfg. Building from source needs ncurses; the 2.0.21 news item says the configure/makefile was restructured around that dependency. No accounts or special hardware are needed.
brief.standout: Unlike most hex editors, it combines a format-aware loader and disassembler for many executable formats with an interactive analyser that stores labels, xrefs and comments per file. It also has a search mode that runs a boolean expression over every offset, for example to flag high-entropy regions that suggest packed or encrypted data.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage's newest item is the HT 2.1.0 release announced 11 January 2015. Later items are only about the move of the source repository to GitHub (September 2014), and nothing newer appears on the homepage. The GitHub README still says 'This is HT 2.1.0'. I could not see commit dates, so I cannot say whether development continues.
brief.caveats: Target systems listed are GNU/Linux, FreeBSD and Win32. The README notes that some keys do not work in HT-posix and suggests using Escape in place of Control. Licensed under GPL version 2. Some formats are still unimplemented (M$-OBJ, ARCH, LX). MZ is disassembly only, and the Flat format has no disassembler. The 0.9.3 news item says Win98 is no longer supported and WinXP is needed. The homepage is dated and was last updated around 2015.
